clue.text: In which a new and lively subject may be given an airing

definitions.text: In which a new and lively subject may be given an airing

parts.words: In which a new and lively subject may be given an airing
parts.note: the 'new and lively subject' sounds like a fresh topic aired in debate, but it is a newborn baby wheeled out for fresh air in a carriage

explanation.surface: A forum where some bright new topic gets aired for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' and 'airing' suggest public debate; the subject is a baby, and the airing is a walk in the park.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby carriage is the vehicle in which an infant is pushed out for fresh air.

clue.text: Table colour-receivers (potty idea!)

parts.note: on a snooker table the coloured balls end up in netted holes; 'potty' hints at potting, sinking a ball

explanation.surface: Something that picks up colour on a table, a daft idea.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker the coloured balls are 'potted' into holes at the table's corners and sides, which is the joke in 'potty'.
explanation.definitionFit: The netted holes on a snooker or billiard table into which balls, including coloured ones, are potted.

clue.text: Writer's request, say

parts.note: a Victorian novelist whose surname looks like the plea any author makes: please peruse my book

explanation.walkthrough: The name of Charles Reade, author of The Cloister and the Hearth, looks like an author asking you to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth, whose surname suggests a plea to peruse.

clue.text: Charybdis, Norwegian style

parts.note: Charybdis was the whirlpool of Greek myth; the clue wants the famous Norwegian whirlpool off the Lofoten Islands

explanation.walkthrough: Charybdis was the whirlpool opposite the monster Scylla; Norway's equivalent gave English its word for a violent vortex.
explanation.definitionFit: A great whirlpool off the Lofoten coast of Norway, the northern counterpart of the mythical whirlpool facing Scylla.

clue.text: Take part in a tie-break

parts.note: sounds like playing in a deciding game, but means helping a knot come apart

explanation.surface: Playing in a deciding game after a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: A tie-break decides a drawn match in sport; here the tie is a knot or necktie, and taking part in its breaking means unfastening it.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or untie a knot, bow or button.

clue.text: Give up Georgia if badly beaten all round

indicators.note: the reworked letters go all the way around the state abbreviation
the letters of beaten are put together badly, out of order

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Surrender Georgia if soundly defeated everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgia looks like the country, but GA is the US state. 'badly' gives ABNETE, which 'all round' wraps around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or deny oneself something, relinquishing it.

clue.text: An ear for music ?

parts.note: an ear is a body part of this kind, and the same word names a keyboard instrument for music

explanation.walkthrough: 'An ear for music' is a talent; read literally, it is a body part that happens to share its name with an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear is a bodily part with a function; the same word is a pipe instrument played in churches.

clue.text: Pacing out about a mile for field operations

indicators.note: the reworked letters go around the letter for a mile
used as in 'out of order', signalling the letters of pacing are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier striding out about a mile across a battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges PACING to CPAIGN, and 'about' puts it around A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of military operations carried out in a particular area or war.

clue.text: About to give up and retire

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in letters
to cede is to give up territory or rights

explanation.surface: Someone ready to surrender and withdraw from public life.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to withdraw or move back, as a tide or hairline does.

clue.text: Bold-faced Edward Hyde

definitions.meaning: the name of a heavy, emphatic typeface used in printing
the seventeenth-century statesman and historian Edward Hyde was created Earl of this title

explanation.surface: A brazen Edward Hyde, as if Jekyll's alter ego.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Hyde evokes Stevenson's Mr Hyde, and 'Bold-faced' seems to describe his shamelessness; in fact it is a printing typeface, and this Hyde is the Stuart-era Lord Chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: The typeface sense names a heavy printing font; the title sense names the earldom held by the historian Hyde.

clue.text: Composer may make a note of her name.

definitions.text: Composer may make a note of her name.

parts.words: Composer may make a note of her name.
parts.note: the girl's name is also the word before 'note' for a short ornamental note a composer writes before a main one

explanation.surface: A songwriter jots down a woman's name to remember it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a note of' reads as 'write down', but the composer makes an ornamental note that bears her name.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name that also labels the musical ornament written as a tiny note before the main one.

clue.text: Very colloquial

parts.note: the two-word phrase is an informal way of saying 'extremely'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Very colloquial' looks like a comment on style; it is a definition of 'very' together with a label saying the phrase is colloquial.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal intensifier used in chatty speech to mean extremely or greatly.

clue.text: Bag a nip, perchance therein lies poetic inspiration

indicators.note: the answer is said to lie inside the preceding words, so it is read straight through them

explanation.surface: Grabbing a quick drink might be where poetic inspiration comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'bAG A NIP PErchance'. Aganippe was a spring on Mount Helicon sacred to the Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the waters of this Helicon spring gave inspiration to poets who drank them.

clue.text: God of the Rings

parts.note: reads like a fantasy title, but means the Roman deity whose name is borne by the planet circled by rings

explanation.surface: A deity ruling over magical rings, as in a fantasy epic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of agriculture gives his name to the sixth planet, famous for its ring system.

clue.text: End of item in a series in America

parts.note: in mathematics a term is one item in a series or sequence
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: The last instalment of a US serial drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' looks like part of 'End of item' but stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stop on a railway or bus line.

clue.text: For Twinkling bet is about right, £1

indicators.note: the word for a wager is said to be around the other letters, wrapping them

parts.note: a stake is a bet
£ is L (from Latin libra, pound) and 1 is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone wagering a pound on the right outcome to win a twinkling prize.
explanation.walkthrough: '£1' gives two letters: the pound sign is L, and 1 is the Roman I; 'is about' sets them, after R, inside the wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Twinkling describes something that glitters like a star in the night sky.

clue.text: Song from a small disc ? Yes

parts.note: a roundel is a small disc, such as an RAF marking
AY (or aye) is an old word for yes

explanation.surface: A tune taken from a little record, and an enthusiastic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: An old short simple song with a refrain, sung in rounds.

clue.text: Our top thinker in church about to go to Birmingham.

indicators.note: the earlier letters travel on to the city's nickname, which follows them

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
RE means about or concerning
Brum is the colloquial name for Birmingham, England's second city

explanation.surface: The cleverest member of a congregation is off to Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUM is Birmingham, England's second city. 'Our top thinker' is the brain's largest part, at the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest part of the human brain, where conscious thought happens, sitting at the top of the skull.

clue.text: Produced uninspired play ?

parts.note: sounds like staging a dull drama, but means playing a guitar by brushing its strings in a mechanical, unimaginative way

explanation.surface: A director put on a lacklustre drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produced' and 'play' suggest theatre; the play is on a stringed instrument, sweeping the strings without finesse.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a guitar or banjo by sweeping across the strings, often idly or without skill.

clue.text: Priest involved in private promotion

indicators.note: means twisted up or entangled, so the letters of priest are mixed

explanation.surface: A clergyman embroiled in a secret career advancement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges PRIEST. 'Private' is a soldier, not 'secret': a private's promotion earns a stripe on the sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier advanced to lance corporal gains a chevron on the sleeve marking his rise in rank.

clue.text: Changed service in a queer duet

indicators.note: the service's letters go inside the reworked letters of duet
used in its old sense of odd or strange, signalling the letters of duet are rearranged

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A naval man altered his part in a strange duet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queer' is used in its old sense of odd; it gives TUED, and 'in' sets the navy inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something altered has been transformed, as milk goes off or a coat is reversed.

clue.text: Sweet with hair put up

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting a word up means reading it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: tressed means having tresses, locks of hair

explanation.surface: A sweet-looking woman whose hair has been pinned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' makes TRESSED read DESSERT. 'Put up' plays on putting hair up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pudding or sweet course served at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Precipitation sounding costly for the herd

annotationWithheld.why: Precipitation sounding costly for the herd: RAIN + DEAR said aloud gives REINDEER, but the one indicator 'sounding' stands between the two words heard, so no single leaf can hold them and two sound ops leave one without an indicator; the grammar cannot express it
annotationWithheld.clue: Precipitation sounding costly for the herd

clue.text: Way-out solution for overtaxed brains

parts.note: sounds like a radical remedy for mental fatigue, but alludes to a 'brain' exodus, and a channel that is literally a way out

explanation.surface: An unconventional remedy for a mind worn out by overwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Scientists leaving Britain in the 1960s to escape high taxes was called the brain ___; also it is a literal way out for water.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe or channel carrying water away, a way out; overtaxed scientists fleeing abroad formed the 1960s 'brain' exodus.

clue.text: —— a fellow of great beauty.

parts.note: the blank is filled by the mythical youth whose name now stands for any very handsome man

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank clue: the missing name completes the phrase as a description of male good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: The youth loved by Aphrodite, a byword for a strikingly handsome man.

clue.text: Word for the occasion

parts.note: sounds like a fitting speech, but means a term coined to be used just once

explanation.walkthrough: A word coined for a single use is called by this name; 'Word for the occasion' is the definition plus a pun on 'just for once'.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off word invented for a single occasion is a ____ word; 'for the ____' means for the present time.

clue.text: "Christian kisses on an 'eathen ——'s foot" (Kipling)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Kipling: the missing word is a carved image worshipped by heathens

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: the blank is the object of worship whose foot the Christian kisses.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved image of a god worshipped by pagans, which the heathen bows before in Kipling's verse.

clue.text: Girl parking in, front of Oxford Hall

indicators.note: the parking letter is placed before the hall's name

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
Aula, Latin for hall, is used in the Latin names of Oxford halls, such as St Edmund Hall (Aula Sancti Edmundi)

explanation.surface: A girl is parking her car outside an Oxford college hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford's St Edmund Hall is formally Aula Sancti Edmundi, so the hall is AULA.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name.

clue.text: Whiff from the east-north-east, colder perhaps

indicators.note: suggests the letters may come out in some other order, an invitation to rearrange

parts.note: ENE is the compass abbreviation for east-north-east

explanation.surface: A wind from the east-north-east brings a chillier smell, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ENE and COLDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent or aroma; a faint smell carried on the air.

clue.text: We must all work to end it

definitions.text: We must all work to end it

parts.words: We must all work to end it
parts.note: reads like a rallying call against some social evil, but literally: if everyone has a job, the condition of being jobless disappears

explanation.surface: A political slogan urging a common effort to defeat a social problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of having no paid job; if all of us have work, there is none.
